newsitem.title: LATVIA: OLAINFARM UNDERLYING Q1 PROFIT 500,000 LATS.
newsitem.headline: OLAINFARM UNDERLYING Q1 PROFIT 500,000 LATS.

text.p: Hansa Investment said on Friday that Olainfarm saw underlying profit of around 500,000 lats during the first quarter and its reported big loss was due to one-off tax debt items.
"The reported net loss includes essentially non-cash non-recurring charges which should not be of great concern, Benjamin Wilson, manager of Hansa Investments, told a news conference.
Hansa organised a sale of shares in Olainfarm to a wide group of investors before the poort Q1 results came out.
Olainfarm reported a net loss after taxation of 1.62 million lats but this was stated after charging items of around 2.14 million lats of a non-recurring nature, Wilson said.
Olainfarm recognised a liability of overdue tax penalties and interest which relates to amounts accrued in previous years, even before 1996, Hansa said.
The one-off items also include write downs of buildings and unfinished construction of 616,000 lats not used by the company, and write downs of debts and other assets of 271,000 lats.
Hansa has two of its representatives included in the Olainfarm board.
Wilson said that a combined solution of rescheduling the debt with the state revenue service and capitalising part of it was being worked on.
Hansa also said a big part of the Olainfarm shares it had earlier acuired had been sold to large foreign investment funds.
Hansa works in close cooperation with the Baltic Republic Fund of Societe General and a number of funds in London.
